([[Westtown, Pennsylvania]]) | college = [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] (2017–2018) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | highlights = *Second-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] (2018) *Big 12 All-Defensive Team (2018) *Big 12 All-Newcomer Team (2018) *[[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2017]]) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport | Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|the {{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|FIBA Americas U18 Championship]]}} {{MedalGold| [[2016 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|2016 Chile]] | [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|National team]]}} }} '''Mohamed Bamba''' (born May 12, 1998) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|University of Texas at Austin]]. He is highly regarded due to his {{height|ft=7|in=10}} wingspan. He attended [[Westtown School]] in [[Westtown Township, Chester County, Pennsylvania|West Chester, Pennsylvania]] and was considered one of the top high school prospects of the class of 2017. ==Early life== Bamba was born on May 12, 1998 in [[Harlem]], [[New York (state)|New York]] to Lancine Bamba and Aminata Bamba, who both emigrated from the [[Ivory Coast]].{{cite web|title=Mohamed Bamba|url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/b/bamba-mohamed-2.aspx|website=''[[USA Basketball]]''|accessdate=April 12, 2017|date=April 11, 2017}}{{cite web|last1=Geoghegan|first1=Neil|title=Westtown star Mohamed Bamba tries to stay cool as spotlight grows brighter|url=http://papreplive.com/2017/02/20/westtown-star-mohamed-bamba-tries-to-stay-cool-as-spotlight-grows-brighter/|website=PA Prep Live|accessdate=April 12, 2017|date=February 20, 2017}}{{cite web|last1=Slater|first1=Andrew|title=Blue Chip: 6'11" 2017 Five-Star Mohamed Bamba|url=http://duke.247sports.com/Article/Blue-Chip-611-2017-Five-Star-Mohamed-Bamba-46129399|website=''[[247Sports.com]]''|accessdate=April 12, 2017|date=July 7, 2016}} Bamba's grandparents were born and brought up in [[Mali]]. His older brother, Sidiki Johnson, played college basketball at [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]], and [[Wabash Valley College|Wabash Valley]].{{cite web|last1=Calle|first1=Franklyn|title=The World is His|url=http://www.slamonline.com/college-hs/the-world-is-his/#YMXwCAEjGaFzoRUd.97|website=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam Online]]|accessdate=April 12, 2017|date=August 4, 2016}} Another member of his family, [[family estrangement|estranged]] half-brother Ibrahim Johnson, also played college basketball at multiple universities, including both [[Farmingdale State College|Farmingdale State]] and [[Montevallo Falcons|Montevallo]],{{cite web|url=http://www.farmingdalesports.com/sports/mbkb/2011-12/bios/14_ibrahim_johnson?view=bio|title=Farmingdale State Athletics|website=Farmingdale State Athletics|accessdate=27 April 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://texas.247sports.com/Article/Exclusive-Elite-Texas-Commit-Mo-Bambas-Longtime-Mentor-Responds--53379813|title=Exclusive: Elite Texas Commit Mo Bamba's Longtime Mentor Responds To Estranged Brother's Allegations|publisher=|accessdate=27 April 2018}} Bamba first became interested in basketball at age six, inspired by the game's popularity in his hometown. ==High school career== [[File:20170329 MCDAAG Mohamed Bamba dunk (2).jpg|thumb|right|Bamba [[Slam dunk|dunking]] during the [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]] In eighth and ninth grade, Bamba attended [[Cardigan Mountain School]], an all-boys boarding school in [[Canaan, New Hampshire]]. Before his sophomore year, Bamba transferred to [[Westtown School]] in [[Westtown Township, Chester County, Pennsylvania|Westtown]], [[Pennsylvania]].{{cite web|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/high_school/20161206_Basketball_preview__Big_men_-_Westtown_s_Bamba_is_among_nation_s_best.html|title=Pa. basketball preview, big men: Westtown's Bamba is among nation's best|publisher=|accessdate=27 April 2018}} As a junior he averaged 14 points, 11 rebounds, and six blocks per game. He played in the [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2017 McDonald's All American Game]] and the [[Nike Hoop Summit]].{{cite web|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2017/mo-bamba-on-mcdonalds-all-american-honor-its-an-unreal-experience-im-in-awe|title=Mo Bamba on McDonald's All American honor: 'It's an unreal experience. I'm in awe'|date=18 January 2017|publisher=|accessdate=27 April 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article143101499.html|title=Bamba, Knox remain undecided heading into Hoop Summit heavy on UK recruits|publisher=|accessdate=27 April 2018}} Bamba was rated as a five-star recruit and was ranked among the top recruits in his class.{{cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/839r|title=Rivals.com|website=n.rivals.com|accessdate=27 April 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://www.scout.com/player/195659-mohamed-bamba|title=Mohamed Bamba, Texas Longhorns, Power Forward|website=247Sports|accessdate=27 April 2018}} His final four schools were [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] and [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]].{{cite web|url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article127527974.html|title=UK in ‘good position’ with five-star basketball recruit Mohamed Bamba|publisher=|accessdate=27 April 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2017/02/23/mohamed-bamba-kentucky-texas-michigan/98301648/|title=Mohamed Bamba recruitment seems too close to call|publisher=|accessdate=27 April 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2017/03/27/um-target-mohamed-bamba-taking-his-time-decision/99703646/|title=UM target Mohamed Bamba taking his time with decision|publisher=|accessdate=27 April 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://www.masslive.com/hoophallclassic/index.ssf/2017/01/hoophall_classic_2017_prospect_4.html|title=Hoophall Classic 2017 Prospects: Mohamed Bamba, Duke and Kentucky recruit, is top uncommitted player in Class of 2017|publisher=|accessdate=27 April 2018}} Ultimately, Bamba chose to play for the [[University of Texas at Austin|University of Texas]] for his college career. Before playing a single game for Texas, his half-brother Ibrahim Johnson posted a 22-minute-long video on [[Facebook]] [[Facebook Live|Live]], talking about how there were some illegal benefits from a Michigan-based investor involved during the decision-making and that he was reporting the information to the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]].{{cite web|url=https://www.burntorangenation.com/basketball/2017/6/29/15892916/mohamed-bamba-brother-ibrahim-johnson-alleges-illegal-benefits-michigan-based-investor-greer-love|title=Mohamed Bamba’s brother alleges illegal benefits from Michigan-based investor|publisher=|accessdate=27 April 2018}} However, the NCAA reported that nothing involved there would ultimately affect Bamba's eligibility for his freshman season.{{cite web|url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2017/06/29/brother-of-prized-texas-recruit-mohamed-bamba-alleges-ncaa-violations-involving-financial-advisor/|title=Brother of prized Texas recruit Mohamed Bamba alleges NCAA violations involving financial advisor|date=29 June 2017|publisher=|accessdate=27 April 2018}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2017}} {{College athlete recruit entry|commitdate=5/18/17|recruit=Mo Bamba|position=[[Center (basketball)|C]]|hometown=Harlem, N.Y.|highschool=[[Westtown School]]|feet=7|inches=1|weight=216|scout stars=5|rivals stars=5|247 stars=5|espn stars=5|espn grade=96}} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = | rivals ref title =Westtown | scout ref title = | espn ref title = | rivals school =Westtown School | scout s = | espn schoolid = | scout overall = 2, 1 ([[Center (basketball)|C]]) | rivals overall = 2, 1 (C) | espn overall = 3, 2 (C), 1 ([[New York (state)|NY]]) | accessdate = | bball = yes }} ==College career== Bamba made his official college debut on November 10, 2017 against [[2017–18 Northwestern State Demons basketball team|Northwestern State]], recording 15 points and 8 rebounds in a blowout win that night. Eight days later, he recorded 13 points, 10 rebounds, and 5 blocks in a blowout win against [[2017–18 Lipscomb Bisons men's basketball team|Lipscomb]]. On December 30, Bamba recorded a season-high 22 points, 15 rebounds, and 8 blocks in a loss to [[2017–18 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]]. On New Year's Day 2018, Bamba would record a then-season-high 16 rebounds with 10 points in a 74–70 overtime win over [[2017–18 Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball team|Iowa State]]. He would record a new career-high in points scored with 25 points scored with 15 rebounds in a 85–72 win over [[2017–18 Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball team|Ole Miss]] on January 27, 2018, five days after recording his previous high of 24 points in a win over Iowa State. On February 17, Bamba would record a new career-high of 18 rebounds with 10 points scored in a 77–66 win over #23 ranked [[2017–18 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team|Oklahoma]], five days after tying his previous career-high of 16 rebounds with 16 points in a close 74–73 double overtime loss to [[2017–18 Baylor Bears basketball team|Baylor]]. At the end of the regular season for Texas, Bamba was named a member of the Big 12's All-Newcomer Team and All-Defensive Team, as well as be named a member of the All-Big 12 Second Team. Following Texas's loss in the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2018 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament]] to [[2017–18 Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball team|Nevada]], Bamba announced his intention to forgo his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]], where he is expected to be a [[NBA draft lottery|lottery]] selection.{{Cite
